LESSON: SOIL ITS RESOURCES

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Environment and
Topic 1.3: Soil its resources

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Soil its resources. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SOIL ITS RESOURCES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Soil its resources helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: SOIL ITS RESOURCES
Soil its resources is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes

What this means
In this part you learn to name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Soil its resources is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil its resources” around your school. (skill: name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Soil its resources to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Soil its resources from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Soil its resources: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Soil its resources?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Soil its resources means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: name the three types of soils on how different samples of soils based on their feel between their fingers characteristics  Learners to observe the particle sizes.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
